title: Capital Region to host ghost investigations, tours
excerpt: With fall at our doorstep, businesses and local groups are organizing paranormal investigations and ghost tours in true spookyseason fashion.
content:
ALBANY, N.Y. (NEWS10) — With fall at our doorstep, businesses and local groups are organizing paranormal investigations and ghost tours in true spooky-season fashion. For the brave, tickets are available for an afternoon or evening of searching for souls beyond the grave.

Albany Ghost Tour

With the New York Capitol being full of rich history, some souls remain above ground. US Ghost Adventures offers an Albany ghost tour that highlights real hauntings, mysteries, and stories of the spirits still roaming the Capitol.

Tours gather outside the New York State Capitol building on Washington Avenue and last an hour over a one-mile walking route. Tickets cost $26 and can be purchased online through the US Ghost Adventure website. Attendees must present valid identification and can also rent an EMF reader while purchasing their tickets for $7.

Haunted History Paracon at Empty Pocket Ranch

Empty Pocket Ranch in Cobleskill is hosting a one-day immersive experience for the daring. The ranch’s Haunted History Paracon is from 9 a.m, to 4 p.m. on September 19.

The day includes guest appearances from Netflix’s “True Haunting” host Chris Dicesare and other paranormal researchers like Jack Kenna and Steve Kulls. Plenty of vendors are also lined up to attend and sell metaphysical items, books, and other unique finds. Tickets are $20 in advance online or $25 at the door, while kids 12 and under are free.

Saratoga County Homestead

Although all of Haunted Nights’ overnight investigations at the Saratoga County Homestead are sold out, a few tickets are still available for a special Halloween tour.

The afternoon tours are of the homestead’s basement, first floor, and second floor. Each tour is two hours long, and attendees are encouraged to plan accordingly, as there are no bathrooms.

Tours are still available from 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. and from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. Tickets are $30 and can be purchased online through the Haunted Nights website.

Fort Fright in Lake George

From September 24 through October 30, Fort William Henry in Lake George will host Fort Fright, a new haunted house experience this fall. The event also features mini paranormal investigations of the fort’s extensive history and legends.
